proposals.after: During the Dashun era the Martial Emperor's general Li Cunxiao, having pacified Xing and Ming, proposed to the Martial Emperor that Zhen and Ding be seized together, and for years thereafter led campaigns harassing the counties under Zhen.
proposals.reason: 大順 is Dashun, not Dazhun.

proposals.before: The Bian general Zhang Cunjing attacked the city with scaling ladders and battering rams massed like clouds. Chuzhi mounted the wall and called out, "Our humble district has never been disloyal to the court nor discourteous to neighboring prefectures. Why did we not expect Your Lordship to enter our land?"
proposals.after: The Bian general Zhang Cunjing attacked the city with scaling ladders and battering rams massed like clouds. Chuzhi mounted the wall and called out, "Our humble district has never been disloyal to the court nor discourteous to neighboring prefectures. I did not expect Your Lordship to enter our land—why?"
proposals.reason: 不虞君之涉吾地，何也 means surprise at the invasion, not self-blame for failing to expect it.

decisions.reason: Focus unit opens 大順中; 順 is shùn, so Dashun is the correct era name and Dazhun is a false reading. The proposed idiomatic line otherwise matches the Chinese.
Same era name error in the literal field: 大順 must be Dashun, not Dazhun; the rest of the proposed literal sentence is faithful.
Chinese 鎔於昭宗朝 treats Rong and Zhaozong as distinct; without the comma English 'Emperor Zhaozong Rong' fuses them into one name. The comma fixes that real ambiguity without changing meaning.
Literal field has the same fusion of Zhaozong and Rong; 鎔於昭宗朝 requires separating the emperor's reign from Rong as subject.

不虞君之涉吾地，何也 states surprise that the addressee entered the land and asks why; the original English wrongly turns this into self-blame about failing to expect the invasion. The proposed rendering matches the Chinese.
Literal likewise misreads 不虞…何也 as 'why did we not expect'; the Chinese asserts unexpected invasion and questions the reason. The replacement is accurate.
既至湖湘 refers to the Hunan (Dongting–Xiang) region, not Hunan plus Hubei; the idiomatic already has Hunan, and dropping Hubei from the literal restores the Chinese scope.
付段佪 names Duan Huai (佪 = huái); Duan Si invents a wrong given name. The added comma after Tiancheng is needed English punctuation and does not alter sense.
Literal repeats the false name Duan Si for 段佪; Duan Huai is correct, with the comma after the reign phrase.
Short-form subject 佪 continues 段佪 from the prior unit; English Si does not match that given name, while Huai does.
Literal likewise mistranslates 佪 as Si; the short form is Huai, continuing 段佪.
